_meta.source: In-game Notice 'Update Log' for Version 1.1.9 of Archero 2 — eight screenshots captured by XYIAN (Kyle) on 2026-09-17 and transcribed verbatim at docs/game-knowledge/updates/2026-09-17-version-1.1.9.md. The notice was live in game on 2026-09-17 and prints no release date of its own; its Arena and Dragoon items are written in the future tense ('will be restructured', 'once changes go live', 'takes effect as soon as the version releases'), so the notice alone does not date the release. Kyle (guild owner) reported on 2026-09-17 that the game had received the update; that report is the basis for treating Version 1.1.9 as released by 17 September 2026. The Notice carousel alternates a 'Version 1.1.9' banner and a 'Hotfix' banner over one continuous Update Log (New Content, Rumble Ladder Improvements, Arena Improvements, Guild Raid Improvements, Gameplay Optimizations, Bug Fixes).
_meta.confidence: high for everything the notice states verbatim; every fact here traces to the transcript. Where an entry goes beyond the notice it is worded as a reading, not as a notice statement: the two skins are filed as character skins because the notice names each skin's owner; Starbound Eternity is filed as a Guild Expedition league because season_rewards already calls that ladder 'tiers' and the name follows the -bound pattern; 'Sprite damage' is glossed from this knowledge base's own Sprite entries; 'camps' is printed as-is. Where the notice names something without saying what it is (Starfall Disc, Fullmoon Pool, King Fisher Tickets, Dragon Gate Koi, Starbound Eternity, Football Rumble, Cred Score, Nian Beast, the Seraph boss, the Wheat Field skill, the Sword Strike affixes, Interdimensional Cores, Tidal and Razor Starcore-SPEC, Artemis, Demeter) the entry says what the notice says and that the rest is not documented, pointing at !suggest. Dates are absolute with year 2026 and UTC times as printed. The rule 'These changes apply to the standard Arena only and do not affect Peak Arena. Anything not noted otherwise takes effect as soon as the version releases.' is printed in italics at the foot of the Arena Improvements section only (screenshot 39399398, before the Guild Raid Improvements heading); the other sections carry no such line, and the log ends at Bug Fixes item 7 with no closing rule (screenshot d7d30661). The release date is not printed; the guild owner's report dates the update to 17 September 2026 at the latest (see source). The future-dated items are Angler's Bounty Special Edition (19 September to 2 October 2026), the Arena matchmaking-range change (21 September 2026, 0:00 UTC), the Guild Expedition season with the Starbound Eternity tier (5 October 2026, no time printed) and the All-Star Cup / Mega All-Star Cup 'Plant build' season (5 October 2026, 0:00 UTC). Every repaired value keeps the still-true facts of the old value and dates the superseded ones as history. Pre-1.1.9 Dragoon and Meteor material carries the same 'recorded before Version 1.1.9' caveat everywhere it appears: weapons.pve_vs_pvp_rankings, gear_sets.pvp_mixed_set.text and the 'For PvP mixed set' custom fact for Dragoon; runes.etched_meteors and the partial Meteor Split ladder custom fact for Meteor runes. Every notice item has a structured entry — cosmetic previews under main_screen.cosmetic_previews, Bug Fix 1 under main_screen.home_screen_animation_fix_1_1_9, Football Rumble quick emotes under game_modes.arena.football_rumble_quick_emotes — so the custom facts carry only a version fact, a one-paragraph headline list of what is new, and the seven bug fixes; per-item detail lives in the structured entries, which keeps one source of truth per item. Spelling: the notice writes 'Transcendant'; main_arena_tiers states once that the older 'Transcendent' spelling names the same tier, and the new tier names use the notice's spelling. Every 1.1.9 fact says 'Version 1.1.9', never 'the hotfix', because fourteen existing facts own 'the August 2026 hotfix' and the 1.1.9 carousel also shows a 'Hotfix' banner. The August 2026 hotfix's version number is still unrecorded (custom fact of 2026-08-28 stays true) — nothing here calls it 1.1.8.

events.fishing: Fishing is one of the most recurring events, happening almost every month. It is one of the main ways to obtain etched runes. Players should prioritize fishing events when they appear. The Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice, captured 17 September 2026, names a fishing event 'Angler's Bounty Special Edition' running 19 September 2026 to 2 October 2026 inside the Starmoon Vow series — see anglers_bounty_special_edition. Whether the regular monthly fishing event is itself called Angler's Bounty is not stated in the notice.
events.starmoon_vow: Starmoon Vow is the Mid-Autumn Special Event Series announced in the Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice, captured 17 September 2026. It lasts 2 weeks and has four parts: (1) Angler's Bounty Special Edition — a fishing event with the special fishing zone Fullmoon Pool (a higher chance of landing King Fisher Tickets) and the all-new Epic Mystling Dragon Gate Koi, event period 19 September 2026 to 2 October 2026; (2) Starfall Disc — win the festival-limited Legendary skins Artemis's 'Moonwake Shimmer' and Demeter's new skin 'Silkveil Harvest'; (3) a 7-Day Sign-in; (4) Alliance Treasure rewards. The 19 September to 2 October 2026 period is printed under Angler's Bounty Special Edition only; the notice gives no separate dates for the other three parts beyond the series lasting 2 weeks. How each part is played and what it rewards beyond the named skins and Mystling are not documented — say so and point at !suggest. Starmoon Vow is not the Starlight Gala (a guild feature), not the Starlight Cup / All-Star Cup (arena), and not Starbound Eternity (a Guild Expedition tier).
events.anglers_bounty_special_edition: Angler's Bounty Special Edition is the fishing event in the Starmoon Vow series (Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice, captured 17 September 2026). Event period: 19 September 2026 to 2 October 2026 (printed 09/19-10/02, month/day). It features the special fishing zone Fullmoon Pool, which has a higher chance of landing King Fisher Tickets, and it brings the all-new Epic Mystling Dragon Gate Koi. What King Fisher Tickets are spent on is not documented, and whether they are the same thing as the 'golden tickets' or 'silver tickets' in the community fishing note is not documented — do not treat them as the same. Whether the regular monthly fishing event is itself named Angler's Bounty is not stated.
events.fullmoon_pool: Fullmoon Pool is the special fishing zone of Angler's Bounty Special Edition during Starmoon Vow, 19 September 2026 to 2 October 2026 (Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice, captured 17 September 2026). Fishing there has a higher chance of landing King Fisher Tickets. How Fullmoon Pool is unlocked and what else it drops are not documented — say so and point at !suggest. It is a fishing zone, not the Serenity Pool campaign map.
events.starfall_disc: Starfall Disc is one of the four parts of the Starmoon Vow event series (Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice, captured 17 September 2026): in it you can win festival-limited Legendary skins — Artemis's 'Moonwake Shimmer' and Demeter's new skin 'Silkveil Harvest' (see the skins category). Both are named as belonging to a character, so they are recorded under skins as character skins; the notice does not use the words character skin or weapon skin. How Starfall Disc is played, what it costs, and its exact dates within the 2-week series are not documented — say so and point at !suggest. Starfall Disc is a Starmoon Vow event, not guild content (Starlight Gala) and not arena content (All-Star Cup).
events.starmoon_vow_7_day_sign_in: Starmoon Vow includes a 7-Day Sign-in with rewards (Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice, captured 17 September 2026). This is an event sign-in inside the 2-week Starmoon Vow series and is separate from the regular Daily Sign-in, which has run on a 28-day cycle since update 1.1.7 — the notice does not say the regular Daily Sign-in changed. The 7-Day Sign-in's rewards and exact dates are not documented.
events.starmoon_vow_alliance_treasure: Starmoon Vow includes Alliance Treasure rewards (Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice, captured 17 September 2026). Alliance Treasure was earlier recorded as one of the Rick and Morty collab's limited-time features, so it appears in more than one event and is not collab-exclusive. What Alliance Treasure is, what the Starmoon Vow rewards are, and whether the guild-membership requirement recorded for the collab's Alliance Treasure also applies here are not documented — say so and point at !suggest.

campaign.hard_vs_heroic_naming: Hard Mode and Heroic Mode are TWO NAMES FOR THE SAME campaign track — the harder second track that runs alongside the Normal Mode chapters. Chapter numbering is one continuous sequence across both names: update 1.1.7 added 166-175, the August 2026 hotfix (previewed 2026-08-23, official notes 2026-08-28) added 176-185, and Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026) added 186-195. A question about 'Heroic chapter N' and 'Hard chapter N' means the same stage.
campaign.stage_ranges_august_2026: The August 2026 hotfix added Campaign (Normal) stages 191-200 and Hard stages 176-185. Official patch notes, 28 Aug 2026. These are no longer the newest chapters: Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026) added Campaign chapters 201-210 and Hard Mode chapters 186-195 — see stage_ranges_version_1_1_9.
campaign.difficulty_reductions: Three SEPARATE difficulty reductions, all true and none replacing another: update 1.1.7 lowered the difficulty of campaign stages after Chapter 80; the August 2026 hotfix lowered it for campaign stages after Chapter 130; and Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026) lowered it for Campaign stages past Chapter 100. The newest of the three is the Version 1.1.9 reduction past Chapter 100. The notice does not say how the three reductions combine.
campaign.stage_ranges_version_1_1_9: Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026) added new Campaign chapters 201-210 and new Hard Mode chapters 186-195, and reduced the difficulty of Campaign stages past Chapter 100. As of 17 September 2026 these are the newest Campaign (Normal / Main) and Hard (Heroic) chapters recorded here; they extend the 191-200 and 176-185 ranges added by the August 2026 hotfix. The notice does not print the version's release date; XYIAN (the guild owner) reported the update as received on 17 September 2026.

dungeon.shackled_jungle_stage_ranges: Shackled Jungle stages are numbered in one continuous sequence. Update 1.1.7 added stages 1501-1700 (the 1.1.7 note called them 'chapters' — same thing), and Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026) added stages 1701-2150, so 2150 is the highest Shackled Jungle stage recorded here as of 17 September 2026. Earlier ranges are not recorded.

in_run.again_button: The pause screen has an 'Again' button, added in Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026), in Campaign, All-Star Cup and Mega All-Star Cup official matches: it lets you retry by spending Energy or a Ticket. Which ticket, and what counts as an 'official match' in the two cups, are not stated in the notice — say so if asked.
in_run.free_skill_discards: Since Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026), players can discard skills for free 3 times per day. The notice does not say which modes this covers, what a discard costs after the third, or whether 'discard' is the same action as a skill refresh (Tactics Talent Card, Monthly Card) or the Monthly Card's 'forfeit skill selection' — do not equate them; if asked, say the relationship is not documented and point at !suggest.
in_run.seraph_boss_strength_reduced: Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026) 'reduced strength of Seraph boss' (the notice's words). The notice lists no change to the hero Seraph (the Epic hero with the Divine Favor skill in the characters category); whether that boss is related to the hero is not stated. Which mode the Seraph boss appears in and what 'strength' was reduced are not stated — point at !suggest.
in_run.revival_screen_countdown_fix: Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026) fixed the revival screen counting down faster than it should.

arena.main_arena: The main arena is the standard 1v1 Arena (the Version 1.1.9 notice calls it the 'standard Arena'). Version 1.1.9 restructures it into 8 tiers — Bronze, Gold, Diamond, Master, Transcendant I, Transcendant II, Supreme I, Supreme II — with Supreme II the top; the notice (captured 17 September 2026) says the rework takes effect as soon as the version releases and prints no release date. Before the rework it had 6 tiers with Supreme as the single top tier (see main_arena_tiers). Standard 1v1 PvP. Peak Arena is a different mode and is not affected by the Version 1.1.9 Arena changes.
arena.all_star_cup: All Star Cup is a PvP tournament mode (recorded as a then-recent addition when this entry was written; Mega All-Star Cup was named alongside it by August 2026). Each season lasts about 12 days and features different bonuses for different runes and loadouts. Depending on the active season's bonuses and your loadout, you could dominate or struggle — adapting your build to the season's modifiers is key. When selecting a start time, Habby made the time slots actually localized for players.
arena.main_arena_tiers: Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026; the notice says the rework takes effect as soon as the version releases and prints no release date) restructures the standard Arena (Main Arena, 1v1) into 8 tiers, low to high: Bronze, Gold, Diamond, Master, Transcendant I, Transcendant II, Supreme I, Supreme II. Supreme II is the top tier. The notice spells it 'Transcendant'; older entries here spell it 'Transcendent' — both spellings name the same tier. When the rework first goes live, players in the old Transcendant tier move to Transcendant I and players in the old Supreme tier move to Supreme I; no one is placed directly into Transcendant II or Supreme II based on their points before the rework. The notice gives no group sizes or promotion/demotion quotas for the 8 tiers. If a member's game still shows the 6 tiers below, the version has not reached their client yet. Before the rework there were 6 tiers, low to high, with these observed rules: Bronze: 50 players per group, top 15 promoted. Gold: 100 per group, top 30 promoted, bottom 40 demoted. Diamond: 200 per group, top 20 promoted, bottom 100 demoted. Master: no group limit, top 20% promoted, bottom 40% demoted. Transcendent (then a single tier): no limit, top 20% promoted, bottom 40% demoted. Supreme (then the single top tier): no promotion possible - the top 40% keep their tier and the rest are demoted. Whether those quotas still apply after the rework, and how promotion works between the I and II tiers, is not documented — point at !suggest. This applies to the standard Arena only, not Peak Arena.
arena.main_arena_settlement: Weekly settlement — the season-end promotion/demotion pass, recorded before the Version 1.1.9 tier rework. If a group holds fewer players than expected, results are assigned in priority order: same-ranked players, then promoted players, then demoted players. The in-game example is a 45-player group where 20 first stay at the same rank, then the top 20 are promoted, then the last 5 are demoted. This is different from the points settlement in the Version 1.1.9 notice's points-rule item, where 'settlement uses the win and loss points fixed in the opponent list' (the notice's words — see main_arena_points_rules).
arena.all_star_cup_seasons: Themes change every season. Sword Strike was the theme when this was first recorded (community notes contributed 4 August 2026). The next All-Star Cup and Mega All-Star Cup season theme is Plant build, starting 5 October 2026 at 0:00 UTC (Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice, captured 17 September 2026 — see all_star_cup_plant_build_season). Which theme runs between that snapshot and 5 October 2026 is not recorded. Build a Preset loadout aligned to the active theme for tournament viability.
arena.main_arena_mechanics: 1v1 ranked PvP ladder on weekly seasons that settle and reset on a 7-day cycle. Challenge attempts are limited (snapshot showed 'Challenge x1', apparently daily-restored); challenge attempts are a different thing from refreshing the challenge list, which from Version 1.1.9 is free for the first two refreshes (see main_arena_challenge_list_refresh). Runs one of your 8 saved preset loadouts. The screen header is named after your current tier, e.g. 'Transcendent Battle' — observed before the Version 1.1.9 tier rework, when Transcendent was a single tier; from Version 1.1.9 the tier names are Transcendant I / II and Supreme I / II, and the header wording for those has not been observed.
arena.all_star_cup_mechanics: Periodic 3-stage tournament with themed seasons (Sword Strike Season at the original snapshot; a 'Plant build' season starts 5 October 2026 at 0:00 UTC per the Version 1.1.9 notice — see all_star_cup_seasons). You must have reached Campaign Chapter 15 to take part in any cycle. Servers are grouped into zones by launch schedule and estimated participant count to balance competition.
arena.mega_all_star_cup: Mega All-Star Cup is a DIFFERENT name from All-Star Cup: it is named beside All-Star Cup in the official August 2026 notice, which also writes it as 'Super All-Star Cup' — both spellings are official and mean this one thing. It receives the same battle change as All-Star Cup (no Boss death animations; the stage timer pauses while selecting a Boss). The Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice (captured 17 September 2026) also names it beside All-Star Cup: both get the Plant build season theme from 5 October 2026 at 0:00 UTC, both get the 'Again' retry button on the pause screen in official matches, and both had the Nian Beast boss's flame-trail bug fixed. How it relates to All-Star Cup — separate mode or higher tier — how you enter it, and what it rewards are all still unrecorded. Never describe it as simply 'the All-Star Cup'.
arena.arena_shop_promised_ruin_shovel: The Promised Ruin Shovel was added to the Arena Shop in the August 2026 hotfix (official patch notes, 28 Aug 2026); its price and daily limit were not given. The arena_shop item list here predates that addition.
arena.rumble_ladder: Rumble Ladder is a PvP ladder mode under Arena. Since Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026) it also has a mode shortcut on the Home screen (the main screen); the notice does not say where on the Home screen the shortcut sits.
arena.rumble_modes: Rumble Ladder modes recorded here: Rumble Dome, Free-for-All, and Football Rumble. The same capture also records Rumble Dome as a trophy-tier name (see rumble_tiers); whether Rumble Dome is a sub-mode, a tier, or both is unresolved. Rumble Dome: ATK and HP scale with your current power. Free-for-All: everyone uses default ATK and HP, and only appearance and Rumble-specific skills are inherited, so gear and runes create no power gap - a pure skill match. Football Rumble: named under Rumble Ladder Improvements in the Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice (captured 17 September 2026), which mentions kickoff, goals and own goals in its matches but does not describe its rules, how you enter it, or what it rewards — those are not documented; say so and point at !suggest (see football_rumble).
arena.rumble_schedule: Rumble Ladder (the whole mode; its in-game Rules screen calls it 'Free-For-All Rumble', which is not the same thing as the Free-for-All sub-mode) is only open during fixed UTC windows. From Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026) mode availability is 1:00:00-4:59:59 and 10:00:00-17:59:59 UTC (UTC+0) — about 12 hours a day. The notice lists this under Rumble Ladder Improvements without naming a sub-mode, and it says nothing about days of the week. Before Version 1.1.9 the in-game Rules screen (recorded August 2026) gave Mon-Wed only, in four 3-hour windows totalling about 36 hours a week; those windows are superseded and are not repeated here. Whether the Mon-Wed restriction still applies is unconfirmed since Version 1.1.9 — say so if asked which days.
arena.rumble_ladder_mechanics: 6-player free-for-all PvP survival, run in periodic seasons (Off-Season at snapshot). Matches last 3 minutes: collect EXP to gain power, defeat monsters to earn gifts, and deliver gifts to storage zones to score points, competing for top rank inside the 3 minutes. This describes the gift-delivery match as recorded from the in-game Rules screen, which the capture applied to the two sub-modes it listed (Rumble Dome and Free-for-All). Football Rumble, which the Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice (captured 17 September 2026) names but does not explain, postdates that capture — whether it uses these rules is not documented.
arena.standard_arena_naming: 'Standard Arena' is the Version 1.1.9 notice's name for the 1v1 ranked Arena that this data calls Main Arena or 1v1 Arena — one mode, three names. Peak Arena (3v3), Rumble Ladder, All-Star Cup and Mega All-Star Cup are different modes, and the Version 1.1.9 Arena Improvements apply to the standard Arena only.
arena.main_arena_changes_version_1_1_9: The Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice (captured 17 September 2026) lists six 'Arena Improvements', all for the standard Arena (Main Arena, 1v1) only and none affecting Peak Arena: (1) Tier System Rework to 8 tiers (see main_arena_tiers); (2) matchmaking range improvements, effective 21 September 2026 at 0:00 UTC (see main_arena_matchmaking_ranges); (3) points rule improvements (see main_arena_points_rules); (4) a new repeat opponent filter (see main_arena_repeat_opponent_filter); (5) defense loss protection (see main_arena_defense_loss_protection); (6) challenge list refresh changes (see main_arena_challenge_list_refresh). The section ends with the rule that anything not noted otherwise takes effect as soon as the version releases; the notice prints no release date; XYIAN (the guild owner) reported the update as received on 17 September 2026, and a member whose Arena tier list still shows six tiers has not received it yet. Only the matchmaking range change carries its own date.
arena.main_arena_matchmaking_ranges: From 21 September 2026 at 0:00 UTC, standard Arena (Main Arena) matchmaking ranges are improved to even out uneven competitive pressure across matchmaking ranges for a better overall experience (Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice, captured 17 September 2026). The notice does not say what the ranges are. This is the one Arena change in the notice with its own effective date. It applies to the standard Arena only, not Peak Arena, and is unrelated to Rumble Ladder's Cred Score matchmaking or to Guild Expedition matchmaking.
arena.main_arena_points_rules: Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026) changed standard Arena (Main Arena) points: challenge points are set by the actual points gap between the two sides, and 'settlement uses the win and loss points fixed in the opponent list' (the notice's words). The notice says this improves cross-server arena matchmaking and points calculation; the exact formula is not given, and it does not say whether that settlement is per battle. This is the points settlement of challenges, not the weekly season promotion/demotion settlement (see main_arena_settlement). Standard Arena only, not Peak Arena.
arena.main_arena_repeat_opponent_filter: From Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026), after you beat the same opponent twice in one day in the standard Arena (Main Arena), that player is no longer recommended when you refresh the challenge list. Standard Arena only, not Peak Arena.
arena.main_arena_defense_loss_protection: From Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026) the standard Arena (Main Arena) has daily protection against point loss on defense: once your accumulated loss meets the protection threshold, further failed defenses cost no points. The threshold value is not given in the notice. This is about Arena defense (other players attacking your defending loadout), not Magic Plant Defense. Standard Arena only, not Peak Arena.
arena.main_arena_challenge_list_refresh: From Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026), refreshing the standard Arena (Main Arena) challenge list: the first two refreshes are free, and the refresh cost resets after you complete a challenge. The notice says this improves the cross-server arena refresh experience; what a refresh costs after the free ones is not given. Refreshing the list is separate from your limited daily challenge attempts, and 'challenge' here means an Arena battle, not the Challenge category (Sky Tower, Seal Battle, Magic Plant Defense). Standard Arena only, not Peak Arena.
arena.peak_arena_unchanged_by_version_1_1_9: Nothing in the Version 1.1.9 'Arena Improvements' (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026) changes Peak Arena. The 8-tier rework, matchmaking range change, points rule changes, repeat opponent filter, defense loss protection and challenge list refresh changes apply to the standard Arena (Main Arena, 1v1) only and do not affect Peak Arena.
arena.all_star_cup_plant_build_season: The next All-Star Cup and Mega All-Star Cup season theme is Plant build, starting 5 October 2026 at 0:00 UTC (Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice, captured 17 September 2026, which prints the date as 10/05). Both cups share this theme. 'Plant build' is the theme's name as printed; what bonuses the Plant build season gives and how long it runs are not stated in the notice — point at !suggest. The knowledge base separately records a Plant rune build pattern under runes.build_patterns.plant_build; the notice does not say the season theme boosts those runes. This is not the Guild Expedition season that also opens on 5 October 2026 — different mode, different content.
arena.nian_beast_boss: Nian Beast is a boss that appears in All-Star Cup and Mega All-Star Cup. Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026) fixed an issue where the Nian Beast boss's flame trail was not cleared when it passed through a room. Nothing else about the Nian Beast boss is documented — point at !suggest. It is not the 'Nian Slayer - Prosperity' / 'Nian Slayer - Longevity' weapon skins in the Skin Exchange Shop.
arena.football_rumble: Football Rumble is part of Rumble Ladder: the Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice (captured 17 September 2026) lists it under Rumble Ladder Improvements. What the notice states: in Football Rumble, scoring 3 or more own goals in a single match costs you Cred Score, and once your Cred Score is low further penalties are applied on top; quick emotes can be sent at kickoff and after a goal. The notice does not describe Football Rumble's rules, how you enter it, or what it rewards — those are not documented; say so and point at !suggest. The notice does not say whether Football Rumble uses the gift-delivery rules recorded under rumble_ladder_mechanics.
arena.rumble_cred_score: Cred Score is the multiplayer score that Rumble Ladder matchmaking uses to prioritise players of similar rank; it is a different number from Trophies (see rumble_trophies). Since Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026), scoring 3 or more own goals in a single Football Rumble match costs Cred Score, and once your Cred Score is low further penalties are applied on top. The notice does not say how much Cred Score is lost, what counts as low, or what the further penalties are.
arena.rumble_match_intro_charm: Since Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026), at the start of a Rumble Ladder match the three players with the highest Charm are shown in an intro animation. Charm is raised by obtaining designated appearances (see the Charm system 2.0 fact). No gameplay effect of this intro is documented.
arena.rumble_results_mvp: Since Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026), the Rumble Ladder results screen shows the match MVP and match statistics. This MVP is per Rumble Ladder match; it is not the weekly guild MVP named at the Starlight Gala. How the match MVP is chosen and which statistics are shown are not documented.
arena.rumble_tiers: Rumble Dome is recorded here as one named trophy tier (range 500-549 observed) and under rumble_modes as a sub-mode name — the same capture says both, and whether Rumble Dome is a sub-mode, a tier, or both is unresolved. Tier gem rewards recorded for Rumble Dome: trophies 10-19 give 240 gems, 30-39 give 400, 40-49 give 400. The 20-29 and 50-59 rows were not captured, and tier names above Rumble Dome are unknown.
arena.main_arena_promotion_note: Recorded before the Version 1.1.9 tier rework (6-tier Arena): the source's own summary table also stated 'Top 46 promote at season settlement', which did not line up with the per-tier promotion rules recorded as the pre-rework quotas under main_arena_tiers. Recorded as written; unresolved and not re-checked after the 8-tier rework.
arena.football_rumble_quick_emotes: From Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026), in Football Rumble quick emotes can be sent at kickoff and after a goal. Which emotes, and whether the other Rumble Ladder sub-modes have them, are not stated (see football_rumble).

game_modes.events_tab: The Events tab groups three categories: Arena (Main Arena, Peak Arena, Rumble Ladder, All-Star Cup and Mega All-Star Cup — see arena.overview), Challenge (Magic Plant Defense, Seal Battle, Sky Tower) and Dungeon (Abyssal Tide, Gold Cave, Shackled Jungle). Each sub-feature has its own season or cycle, rewards and shop.
game_modes.event_shop_currencies: Every Arena mode has its own shop and currency, so running them all yields different shard pools: Arena Coins for Phynx and Nezha shards, Peak Arena Coins for Loki shards, All-Star Cup tokens for Universal Artifact Shards, Rumble Tokens for the Rumble Shop (see arena.rumble_shop); the Mega All-Star Cup shop and currency are not documented.

main_screen.hub_entry_points: The main screen (the Home screen) is the hub for everything else: Hunt (a quick-reward alternative to farming stages), Reach (current campaign progress such as 123-50, which opens the clearance rewards), Guild, Camp (Mystlings), Rankings, Task Center, Friends, a Rumble Ladder mode shortcut (added in Version 1.1.9, in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026; its position on the screen is not stated), and the five bottom tabs Shop, Gear, Campaign, Collectible and Events.
main_screen.home_screen_naming: The in-game update notices call this screen the 'Home screen'. Home screen, main screen and main page all mean this same hub screen — answer a 'Home screen' question from the main_screen entries.
main_screen.friends_list_sorting: From Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026) the Friend list can be sorted by chapter progress, Battle Power or last active, in ascending or descending order, to make friends easier to find. Friends is reached from the main screen (Home screen).

top_up.daily_deals_short_on_aurocite: From Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026) the daily deals purchase flow changed: when you are short on Aurocite, confirming the purchase takes you straight to the matching top-up purchase (the notice does not name the top-up; the Aurocite sub-tab of Top Up is the only Aurocite purchase documented here — see shop.top_up.aurocite). The notice does not say which screen it means by 'daily deals' — the Daily Shop tab, the Limited Offer Daily Special, the Wish tab's daily special packs and the Daily Rewards packs are all daily-refreshing and documented separately, so do not assume it is any one of them — and it does not say whether the deal's price still falls back to USD when your Aurocite balance does not cover it (the currency_display_behavior rule beside this entry describes price DISPLAY; this entry describes what CONFIRMING does).

gold.community_weapon_cap: There are 2 main uses for gold: leveling up weapons and purchasing talent cards. Weapon max level was raised from 150 to 200 in an update before Version 1.1.9 (gear level runs 1-200 per gear_sets.gear_levels; the Version 1.1.9 notice of 17 September 2026 does not mention weapon levels). Talent cards can be bought every 10 profile levels; when this was recorded they maxed out at level 50, and whether more were added at level 60 was not yet known — not documented since.

Alliance Treasure is NOT exclusive to this collab: the Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice (captured 17 September 2026) lists Alliance Treasure rewards again as part of the Starmoon Vow Mid-Autumn event series — see game_modes.events.starmoon_vow_alliance_treasure.

guild.hub_buildings: Guild Hall (members, roles, research, leaderboard), Monster Invasion (the daily guild boss battle, MI), Guild Expedition (multi-guild PvP tournament), Shop / Guild Store (hero shards and random Epic runes), Guild Merchant (community bargain mechanic), and Guild Aid. The Starlight Gala was added later and is not in this list. Guild Raid (see guild_raid) is also not in this list; whether it is the same feature as Monster Invasion is not documented.

guild_hall.ui_upgraded_august_2026: The Guild Hall was fully upgraded in the August 2026 hotfix (official patch notes, 28 Aug 2026): an all-new UI bringing guild info, member management and access to all guild modes together in one place. Every OTHER guild_hall detail here describes the pre-upgrade screen — say so when describing the Guild Hall.

monster_invasion.overview: A guild-wide boss battle where members collectively damage a single boss for tiered rewards. Monster Invasion is also called MI. Whether 'Guild Raid' (see guild_raid) is the same feature or a separate mode is not documented; do not answer a Guild Raid question from this entry unless the member says Monster Invasion or MI.

guild_expedition.leagues: The label under each guild's name on the round screen is its league; season_rewards calls the same ladder 'tiers'. The Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice (captured 17 September 2026) announces 'a new tier, Starbound Eternity' for the season opening 5 October 2026; its name follows the Thunderbound/Dragonbound pattern so it is filed here as a league, but the notice does not itself use the word league. Names documented: Thunderbound Oath, Dragonbound, Starbound Eternity. Dragonbound is higher than Thunderbound Oath. Thunderbound Oath spans the 900-1,199 point band; sub-tier range is 100 points. Starbound Eternity comes with rewards to match; the notice does not state its point band or where it sits relative to Thunderbound Oath and Dragonbound. The full league ladder was not captured.
guild_expedition.starbound_eternity_season_october_2026: The next Guild Expedition season opens on 5 October 2026 (Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice, captured 17 September 2026). It adds a new tier, Starbound Eternity, with rewards to match. The notice gives no opening time or time zone for the season (the 0:00 UTC printed beside the All-Star Cup season in the same notice belongs to the cups, not to this), does not state Starbound Eternity's point band, and does not say where it sits relative to Thunderbound Oath and Dragonbound (see leagues). Anything else about Starbound Eternity is not documented — say so and point at !suggest. This is not the All-Star Cup 'Plant build' season that also starts on 5 October 2026 — different mode, different content.
guild_expedition.matchmaking_guild_rankings: Since Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026), Guild Expedition matchmaking shows guild rankings, and the top 50 guilds can display their rank. The notice does not say what this ranking is based on, where the rank is displayed, or whether it is the same leaderboard as the Guild Rankings button in Guild Research. Do not mix it up with the Monster Invasion guild ranking under monster_invasion.guild_ranking, whose rank bands and mail rewards are Monster Invasion rewards, not Guild Expedition ones.
guild_expedition.member_presets: You can view other guild members' presets in Guild Expedition (since 1.1.7). Since Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026), viewing a member's preset also shows related progression info. The notice does not say which progression info is shown. This is the per-member preset, not the deployment presets on the deployment screen.

guild_store.promised_ruin_shovel: The Promised Ruin Shovel was added to the Guild Shop in the August 2026 hotfix (official patch notes, 28 Aug 2026). The notes do not say which sub-tab carries it, what it costs, or what it is used for.

guild_raid.overview: Guild Raid is a guild mode with more than one difficulty: a member starts a raid, it runs within an event cycle, and it ends in a settlement. Beyond that, what Guild Raid is — what you fight, how it is entered, what it rewards, how long an event cycle lasts — is not documented in this knowledge base. Say so and point at !suggest. Sources: the 1.1.7 update notes (Frenzy Challenge) and the Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026.
guild_raid.relation_to_monster_invasion: Whether Guild Raid is the same feature as Monster Invasion (the daily guild boss battle, MI, documented under monster_invasion) or a separate mode is not documented. Do not answer a Guild Raid question with Monster Invasion details, or the reverse; say the relationship is not documented and point at !suggest. If the member says Monster Invasion or MI, answer from monster_invasion.
guild_raid.difficulty_tiers: Guild Raid has difficulty tiers. Frenzy Challenge, added in 1.1.7, is Guild Raid's highest difficulty tier: after clearing the highest difficulty you can push toward tougher goals for more rewards. The names of the other difficulty tiers are not documented.
guild_raid.difficulty_recommendation: Since Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026), Guild Raid recommends a difficulty based on the guild's total Battle Power.
guild_raid.first_time_auto_open: Since Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026): if no one starts a raid within 24 hours of the current event cycle, the next member to open the Guild Raid screen starts one automatically, at the difficulty recommended for the guild's current total Battle Power. The notice does not say how long an event cycle is or who may start a raid manually.
guild_raid.settlement_countdown_and_reminder: Since Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026), Guild Raid shows a settlement countdown, and a reminder once conditions are met (the notice does not say which conditions), so officers can pace the run.

The Version 1.1.9 notice says nothing else about Etched Twinborn Runes: requirements, costs, which Etched runes qualify, and whether the Twinborn rules recorded in this knowledge base before 17 September 2026 apply unchanged to Etched Runes are not documented — point at !suggest. The 1.1.7 note's phrase 'Blessing Twinborn Rune fusion' means this same Twinborn merging (the community custom facts call it Twinborn forging); it is a different action from the Rune Workshop's Fusion, which fuses owned runes into a single higher-rarity rune (runes.rune_workshop) — the two only share the word 'fusion'.

umbral_tempest.season_4_status: Umbral Tempest Season 4 began on 31 August 2026 — the start date given in the official Archero 2 patch notes of 28 Aug 2026. All Season 4 detail here comes from those pre-launch patch notes and describes the season as it was ANNOUNCED, not as observed in play. The Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice of 17 September 2026 mentions the [Umbral Tempest] season only in a bug fix (see sword_strike_affixes_fix); when Season 4 ends is not documented.
umbral_tempest.coverage_caveat: Coverage of Umbral Tempest is thin: everything recorded is Season 4 pre-launch announcement material from the 28 Aug 2026 patch notes, plus one bug fix from the Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice of 17 September 2026 about the Sword Strike buff affixes (see sword_strike_affixes_fix). The event's core loop, currencies, rewards, affixes, season end dates and past seasons are NOT documented. Do not infer general Umbral Tempest mechanics from these notes.
umbral_tempest.sword_will_not_sword_strike: 'Sword Will' is the Ranger's Umbral Tempest Season 4 Class Ability. It is NOT 'Sword Strike', which is a rune theme, an Etched rune family, a Promised Ruins group, an All-Star Cup season theme, and also the name shared by three Umbral Tempest buff affixes — Sword Strike Enchantment, Sword Strike Laser and Sword Strike Hit — that the Version 1.1.9 in-game Notice (captured 17 September 2026) names in a bug fix (see sword_strike_affixes_fix). Different things — do not answer one with the other's data, and do not describe the Sword Strike affixes as Sword Will.
umbral_tempest.sword_strike_affixes_fix: Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026) fixed an issue in the [Umbral Tempest] season where holding the Sword Strike Enchantment, Sword Strike Laser and Sword Strike Hit buff affixes at the same time applied the debuff to the player instead. The notice does not say which season number, what these three buff affixes do, or how they are obtained — none of that is documented; point at !suggest. 'Sword Strike Enchantment' is the name of an Umbral Tempest affix, not the rune Enchantment system, and none of the three is the Ranger's Sword Will Class Ability.

custom_facts.text: Version 1.1.9 is the Archero 2 update announced in the in-game Notice 'Update Log' captured by XYIAN on 2026-09-17 (eight screenshots). The notice was live in game on 2026-09-17 and prints no release date; its Arena and Dragoon items are written in the future tense ('will be restructured', 'once changes go live'), but XYIAN (the guild owner) reported on 2026-09-17 that the game had received the update, so treat Version 1.1.9 as released by 17 September 2026 while remembering that the notice itself prints no date. If a member's game still shows six Arena tiers or no Dragoon version switch, the update has not reached their client yet; the Arena tier list showing Transcendant I / II, or the version number in Settings, is the proof. As of 2026-09-17 it is the newest update recorded here. Version 1.1.9 is a separate, later update from update 1.1.7 and from the August 2026 hotfix, whose official notes of 2026-08-28 give no version number — nothing records which number the August hotfix carried, so do not call it 1.1.8. The Notice carousel also shows a banner labelled 'Hotfix' above the same continuous Update Log; when you mean this update say Version 1.1.9, never 'the hotfix'. The Arena Improvements section ends with the rule that anything in that section not noted otherwise takes effect as soon as the version releases; the other sections carry no such line, and their undated items are simply listed in the Version 1.1.9 notice. The dated items are Angler's Bounty Special Edition (19 September to 2 October 2026), the Arena matchmaking range change (21 September 2026, 0:00 UTC), and the Guild Expedition season and the All-Star Cup Plant build season (5 October 2026; 0:00 UTC stated for the cups only).

What is new in Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026) — a headline list; the per-item entries hold the detail: (1) the Starmoon Vow Mid-Autumn event series, lasting 2 weeks — Angler's Bounty Special Edition fishing with the Fullmoon Pool zone, a higher chance of King Fisher Tickets and the new Epic Mystling Dragon Gate Koi from 19 September to 2 October 2026; Starfall Disc with the festival-limited Legendary skins Moonwake Shimmer (Artemis) and Silkveil Harvest (Demeter); a 7-Day Sign-in; and Alliance Treasure rewards. (2) A new Guild Expedition season on 5 October 2026 with the new tier Starbound Eternity. (3) The All-Star Cup and Mega All-Star Cup 'Plant build' season from 5 October 2026 at 0:00 UTC. (4) Dragoon Set and Meteor build rune balance changes with new affixes, and a switch between the old and new Dragoon Set versions. (5) Etched Twinborn Runes. (6) Campaign chapters 201-210, with difficulty reduced past Chapter 100. (7) Hard Mode chapters 186-195. (8) Shackled Jungle stages 1701-2150. (9) Rumble Ladder improvements: a Home screen shortcut, a Charm intro animation, MVP and match statistics on the results screen, Football Rumble own-goal Cred Score penalties and quick emotes, and availability 1:00:00-4:59:59 and 10:00:00-17:59:59 UTC. (10) Standard Arena improvements that do not affect Peak Arena: an 8-tier rework (Bronze, Gold, Diamond, Master, Transcendant I, Transcendant II, Supreme I, Supreme II), matchmaking ranges from 21 September 2026 at 0:00 UTC, points rules, a repeat opponent filter, defense loss protection, and two free challenge-list refreshes. (11) Guild Raid improvements: a difficulty recommendation from the guild's total Battle Power, first-time auto-open after 24 hours, and a settlement countdown and reminder. (12) Gameplay optimizations: cosmetic previews, an 'Again' retry button in Campaign and both cups, bulk conversion of Interdimensional Cores and Tidal / Razor Starcore-SPEC collab items, Friend list sorting, the daily deals top-up flow when short on Aurocite, reduced Seraph boss strength, 3 free skill discards per day, and Guild Expedition guild rankings (top 50) plus preset progression info. (13) Seven bug fixes, listed in their own fact.

Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026) fixed seven issues: (1) some buttons on the Home screen and tab animations reset incorrectly after switching screens; (2) Phynx's Bleed elemental resistance did not take effect; (3) in All-Star Cup and Mega All-Star Cup the Nian Beast boss's flame trail was not cleared when it passed through a room; (4) the revival screen counted down faster than it should; (5) Mystling Active Skill boosts were not applied to Sprite damage; (6) the visual effect on the Wheat Field skill was softened; (7) in the [Umbral Tempest] season, holding the Sword Strike Enchantment, Sword Strike Laser and Sword Strike Hit buff affixes at the same time applied the debuff to the player instead.

twinborn runes are a new method of merging runes together and can be done from legendary or higher. It essentially merges the two runes into one slot where you can still upgrade and enchant them separately while still merged 

It is expensive to merge and costs both scraps and twinborn cores the scraps is made from salvaging any runes where as twinborn cores are only given from events or buy directly in the store for money or auracrite 

The best event for cores currently is fishing. As you fish and accumulate higher weight, the store unlocks more and more cores to buy for 12800 silver tickets (the primary fishing currency) or the legendary rare currency for catching rare fish which is golden tickets where it requires 5 per core and unlocks about two per 1000k kg
